correctness.rationale: Any nontrivial fixed point has all coordinates strictly in (0,1), by connectivity and positivity. Odds o(s)=s/(1-s) is strictly convex, so an interior fixed point yields u=o(x)<=Gamma W u and complement yields Gamma^-1W analogue; Perron equality would force neighbor-value equality and via odd cycles a constant fixed point impossible if Gamma!=I. Conversely if both radii >1, small positive Perron eigenvectors give monotone strict lower/upper sub- and supersolutions, whose iterates converge. For uniqueness, maximize odds ratio R>1 between two alleged interior fixed points; strict concavity of T_R(s)=Rs/(1+(R-1)s) and equality at an optimizing coordinate force all neighbors to be maximizers with equal values; graph connectivity and odd cycle force constant equilibrium, contradiction. Bracketing gives auxiliary iteration from any interior state. Tang et al Theorems 3 and 4 give almost-sure approach to equilibrium set and endpoint repulsion/convergence; bounded urn increments convert finite-set approach to convergence, yielding unique x*. Independent exact rational triangle equilibrium (3/4,1/4,1/2) and both positive Perron subeigenvector certificates checked. No claim of new stochastic approximation theorem.
